plate_findings.evidence: asymmetric amyotrophy and marked fatty replacement

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 10 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J). A: Panel A is axial T1 muscle MRI from article titled Segmental areas of denervation in post-polio syndrome, captioned as asymmetric amyotrophy with fatty replacement suggestive of Post-Poliomyelitis Syndrome. B: Panel B T1 axial shows fatty replacement in thigh muscles in post-poliomyelitis syndrome case. C: Panel C T1 axial thigh with asymmetric amyotrophy attributed to post-polio syndrome. D: Panel D T1 axial leg shows amyotrophy/fatty replacement in post-polio syndrome. E: Panel E T1 axial leg with amyotrophy/fatty replacement in post-polio syndrome. F: Panel F axial STIR shows hyperintensity involving right vastus lateralis and tibialis anterior in same post-polio patient; atrophy visible, hyperintensity captured as proposed finding. G: Panel G axial STIR shows denervation hyperintensity in post-polio syndrome limb muscles. H: Panel H coronal T1 shows asymmetric neurogenic islands with fatty replacement suggestive...
panels.attribution_text: Braga et al. Segmental areas of denervation in post-polio syndrome.. Arquivos de neuro-psiquiatria 2024. doi:10.1055/s-0044-1779507. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Muscle MRI studies. Axial ( A-E ) and coronal ( H ) T1-weighted MRI shows asymmetric amyotrophy and marked fatty replacement involving bilateral vastus lateralis, right vastus intermedius, left biceps femoris, right vastus medialis, left tibialis anterior, and bilateral heads of gastrocnemius. Axial ( F,G ) and coronal ( I,J ) STIR MRI shows hyperintensity involving right vastus lateralis and tibialis anterior.
in_text_mentions: Electromyography disclosed bilateral chronic lumbosacral denervation and mild acute denervation involving the right lower limb. Neuroimaging studies (brain and spinal MRI) and genetic testing (MLPA test for quantification of SMN1 and SMN2 copy numbers and hereditary neuropathy, non-5q, and other motor neuron disease panels) were normal. Muscle MRI disclosed asymmetric neurogenic muscle “islands” alternating areas with and without fatty replacement ( Figure 1 ), 1 suggestive of Post-Poliomyelitis Syndrome (PPS). 2 3 Muscle MRI is useful to distinguish PPS from other motor neuron diseases. 1 2 3

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Left lateral radiograph of ipsilateral lower limb in polio survivor showing hypoplastic shin and deformed fibula described in-text as post-infection sequelae of childhood poliomyelitis. B: Middle AP radiograph of same ipsilateral lower limb showing thin hypoplastic tibia/fibula and osteoporotic bones attributed in-text to childhood poliomyelitis infection. C: Right clinical photo of legs showing visibly wasted thin ipsilateral lower leg corresponding to post-polio limb atrophy and hypoplasia described as clinical presentation in poliomyelitis survivor.
panels.attribution_text: Sakellariou et al. Peri-implant proximal femur fracture in a poliomyelitis survivor: A surgical and medical challenge.. Clinical case reports 2023. doi:10.1002/ccr3.7465. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: Past medical history, apart from hypertension, dyslipidemia and osteoporosis also included a childhood poliomyelitis infection that had affected the ipsilateral lower limb. Post‐infection, the patient had a hypoplastic shin bone, deformed fibula and osteoporotic skeletal bones (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Real patient standing photo in polio case report showing bilateral knee recurvatum due to quadriceps weakness 3/5, attributed to poliomyelitis by article title and case context. b: Real patient supine photo showing left knee recurvatum and thin limb in known poliomyelitis patient with quadriceps weakness. c: Real patient supine photo showing right knee recurvatum in poliomyelitis case with documented quadriceps weakness. d: Real patient photo showing leg length discrepancy of 3 cm, a vocabulary-defined post-polio limb shortening manifestation in poliomyelitis patient.
panels.attribution_text: Zari et al. Bilateral Total Knee Replacement in a Patient With Poliomyelitis: A Case Report From Eastern Morocco.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.33317. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical images showing a) knee recurvatum compensated by extension of the hip and dorsiflexion of the foot. b) Significant recurvatum in the supine position of the left knee, c) recurvatum of the right knee, and d) 3 cm shortening.
in_text_mentions: had no trauma history. Currently, the patient presented with progressive pain and limited range in both knees. On physical examination, the patient has bilateral valgus and bilateral knee recurvatum of 40°, a shortening of 3 cm of the left lower limb (Figure 1). The quadriceps force of both knees was 3/5. The left knee range of motion (ROM) was 40-0º-60º, while the right knee ROM was 40º-0-80º. Both knees had global laxity (anteroposterior and mediolateral), with more severe on the left side. The patient has a valgus flat foot, more marked on the left. The examination of both hips was normal.
